notes: Model-configuration journeys. The fake runtime serves a single-model registry, so these cover what the picker says about the registry it was given, what selecting does, and the refusal path for a model that offers no effort levels -- not switching between models, which needs a registry with more than one entry. The model name and its description come from the fake runtime rather than from a scenario file, so a journey cannot vary them; the mutation that proves these predicates are specific is opening a different surface and finding them absent.

scenarios.name: The model picker lists the registry and marks which model is answering
scenarios.description: The model picker opened on a single-model registry -- asserts the entry carries the description the registry supplied, its credit column, and the marker showing it is the active model
verify: screen.contains:Served by mock-krs-server so a prompt can reach the fake KRS.
scenarios.observe: The description is the load-bearing assertion: it is supplied by the runtime's model registry, so it cannot be echoed from anything the run typed, and a picker built from a local default rather than the registry would fail on it while still showing a plausible model name. The name itself is deliberately not asserted -- it also sits in the status line, so it would pass with the picker closed. The active marker is what tells a user which model is answering, and the credit column is part of the row a user reads before choosing.

scenarios.name: Selecting a model closes the picker and the next turn still answers
scenarios.description: A model selected from the picker, then an ordinary prompt -- asserts the picker is dismissed and the session goes on to answer, rather than the selection leaving the prompt captured
scenarios.observe: Choosing from a picker has two failure modes and this covers both: the overlay staying up, and the input never being handed back. The confirmation is waited on rather than asserted, so the predicates carry the part after it -- the answered turn proves the prompt still reaches the runtime, and the absent picker chrome proves the overlay released the screen. Both negatives are safe here because the picker is a live region that repaints rather than scrolling away, so its rows do not linger once it closes.

scenarios.name: Effort levels on a model that has none are refused with the way forward
scenarios.description: The effort command issued while a model without effort levels is active -- asserts the refusal names the limitation and tells the user what would let them proceed
verify: screen.contains:Select a model that supports effort levels
scenarios.observe: A command that cannot apply is only well behaved if it says why and what to do instead, so the run waits on the limitation and asserts the remedy -- the half a user acts on, and the half a refusal is likeliest to drop. Keeping them separate means the predicate is not a restatement of the wait. The active model comes from the fake runtime and offers no effort levels, which is what makes this path the deterministic one here.
